`click.prompt` (src/click/termui.py) raises `click.Abort` (i.e. `click.exceptions.Abort`, a subclass of `RuntimeError`).

In `prompt`'s inner `prompt_func` (termui.py ~lines 135-150) the read is wrapped in `except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError): ... raise Abort()` — so both Ctrl+C (`KeyboardInterrupt`) and Ctrl+D/EOF (`EOFError`) are converted into `Abort`. This matches its docstring: "If the user aborts the input by sending a interrupt signal, this function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception." (When input is hidden, it also echoes a newline before raising.) `click.confirm` does the same.

Working on it: a subagent is investigating src/click/core.py so that a required flag that isn't given raises "Missing option" (exit code 2) instead of silently using its default. I'll confirm when the fix is in and the full test suite still passes.

`fs_enc = "ascii"`.

In `src/click/_unicodefun.py`, `_verify_python_env()` does:

```python
try:
    from locale import getpreferredencoding
    fs_enc = codecs.lookup(getpreferredencoding()).name
except Exception:
    fs_enc = "ascii"
```

So if the `locale.getpreferredencoding` lookup (or the `codecs.lookup`) raises any exception, `fs_enc` falls back to the string `"ascii"` — which then triggers the "Python was configured to use ASCII as encoding" RuntimeError path.

`_join_param_hints` returns a string joining each item's `repr()` with `" / "`: `" / ".join(repr(x) for x in param_hint)` (e.g. `['--foo', '-f']` → `"'--foo' / '-f'"`). If `param_hint` is a plain string (or None) it is returned unchanged.

Fixed and verified. Root cause: `_default_text_stdout()`/`_default_text_stderr()` return `None` when `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` is `None` (pythonw/GUI apps), and `echo()` then crashed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'`. Fix: `_compat._make_cached_stream_func` now returns `None` for a `None` source stream, `utils.echo()` returns early when the resolved stream is `None`, and `_termui_impl.ProgressBar`/`pager` fall back to `StringIO()` so their output is discarded instead of crashing. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed — identical to the pre-change baseline (no test broken); a simulated `test_echo_no_streams` (sys.stdout/stderr = None, echo to both) fails before and passes after.
Started a subagent on the `click.Path` symlink-resolution bug in `src/click/types.py`. I'll report when it's fixed and verified.

Fixed and verified. Root cause: `argument()` in `src/click/decorators.py` did `ArgumentClass = attrs.pop("cls", Argument)` inside the returned decorator, mutating the closure's `attrs`, so reusing the same decorator object (e.g. `arg = click.argument("a", cls=CustomArgument)` applied twice, or on a second command) dropped the custom class on every use after the first. Fix: `cls` is now a named keyword parameter bound in the closure (`if cls is None: cls = Argument`) and `attrs` is never mutated — same style `option()` already uses. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed, identical to baseline.

Fixed and verified. An option with both an `envvar` and a `flag_value` now takes its value from the environment variable when set (e.g. `--upper/--lower` with envvar → env value wins); flag/command-line/default paths unchanged. Final full-suite run: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed — no failures.

Fixed and verified. `click.Path(resolve_path=True)` now resolves symlinks (e.g. `/tmp/symtest/link/f.txt` → `/tmp/symtest/real/f.txt`) while `resolve_path=False` leaves the path untouched. Final full-suite run: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed — no failures.

Fixed and verified. A flag's value is now taken from the command's `default_map` when the flag isn't given (`CliRunner().invoke(cli, [], default_map={'flag': True})` → `flag=True`), and command-line use still overrides it. Final full-suite run: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed — no failures.
